items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: And I loved Stevie Wonder of course... and I got a chance then to play with all these people when I was older.

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you, this thought occurred to me in the last couple of days because I visited your website and there’s three particular videos that you had up there of varying kinds of music. And then hearing your set, the way you played and your set list. I wondered if, as a child, you were an extraordinarily curious boy?

I was. I grew up in Michigan and my father played the trumpet and my mother played piano. I had three sisters, they all took piano lessons. And it’s funny because my father also worked at a factory, as many people in Michigan did, but on the weekends played gigs. So when I was a little kid he would take me to his gigs, so I was like really small. And I would go and he usually had a band of one or two saxophones in the band, piano and/or accordion, bass, drums, guitar, you know, and so he would sing and play the…

one of his saxophone players so he was pushing me more towards hey, maybe — would you like to play the saxophone. So one day he brought a saxophone home like you know for a birthday or something like that. And I was quite young so I was starting to sit in with him when I was ten years old. So I was already curious about the music that he played, which was mostly older music like the swing era, like old jazz standards. But then he would also incorporate a couple of rock tunes, because younger people would want to…
